weekly_reviews.forecast_policy: Frozen pregame projections were graded without revision.

late_information_comparison.conclusion: Later information was effectively neutral for score accuracy

weather.finding: No game crossed the approved severe-weather threshold; no calibration inference is available.

patterns.finding: Realised blowouts (7 games) had 11.46-point team-score MAE versus 7.41 in close games and 7.35 in middle-margin games. Large misses were concentrated in extreme scripts, including Chicago-Carolina and Denver-Kansas City; one completed week is insufficient to reweight scoring.

The model underprojected realised 50+ point games by 21.20 points on average and overprojected realised <=41 point games by 10.10 points. This is a useful diagnostic, but the groups are defined after the result and must repeat prospectively before any variance or total-scoring change.

Four games with a material injury margin signal had 9.74-point team-score MAE and 50.0% winner accuracy, versus 8.97 and 66.7% in the other 12. Late information changed only three projections by tiny amounts and no winner; the three matched 05:00/15:00 pairs are descriptive only.

New-team/unproven and secondary-role market props each hit 36.8% (7/19), below projected starters at 45.4% (59/130). TE props were 4/14 and receptions 17/44. Week 1 usage uncertainty is a plausible repeatable source, but the evidence is not yet large enough to change weights.

Prop edges of 7+ units hit 39.3% (24/61), while 3-6.9 unit edges hit 54.5% (12/22). Winner and prop rating buckets were not monotonic. Continue prospective calibration before considering additional shrinkage of extreme prop edges.
No game crossed the approved severe-weather adjustment threshold, so Week 1 provides no evidence for changing weather weights.
All unlined tackle projections were settled neutrally from complete defensive boxes and excluded from betting accuracy. The market-lined tackle sample is too small for a weight change.

recommendations.reason: One 16-game week and three matched 05:00/15:00 pairs do not provide enough independent evidence.
Separate confirmed starters, new-team players, injury replacements and committee roles before reassessing prop shrinkage.
Review pace, turnover and defensive-score contributions without fitting Week 1 noise.
No repeatable weakness is established strongly enough for a model change.

weekly_reviews.sample_policy: Latest frozen snapshot is the authoritative 16-game scorecard; per-snapshot metrics are also retained. Repeated frozen observations are not pooled as independent games.

weekly_reviews.forecast_policy: Frozen pregame projections graded without revision. Week 3 weather and total-selection refinements are prospective only.
weekly_reviews.summary: Final Week 2 game-line review: winners 9-7 (56.3%), spreads 9-7 (56.3%), totals 7-9 (43.8%). The model projected 47.47 points per game versus 40.44 actually scored, an average +7.03 point scoring bias. Weather handling and small total-edge presentation are refined prospectively for Week 3.

weather_review.finding: Four clearly weather-sensitive games averaged a +15.26 point projection-minus-actual total bias and 18.00 point total MAE, versus +4.29 bias and 10.33 MAE in the other 12 games. This supports better weather handling, not a global scoring reweight from one week.
weather_review.week3_change: Use kickoff-hour weather including precipitation probability, precipitation amount, sustained wind and gusts, with graduated penalties rather than a single 60% precipitation threshold.

totals_review.finding: Eight of 16 total selections had model edges below 2 points and went 3-5; edges of at least 2 points went 4-4.
totals_review.week3_change: Below a 2.0 point total edge, show No meaningful edge rather than an Over/Under recommendation.
